### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — TFM condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, line 10

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this solution), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK sets it from `<TargetFramework>` only after the project file's first `<PropertyGroup>` is processed. This condition will **never** be true, so documentation files are never generated despite the apparent intent.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, where `$(TargetFramework)` is populated:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Unconditional property overrides project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–10

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` is imported **after** the project file. Any unconditional property assignment here silently overwrites project-level values. LibB explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` but it is clobbered by this file.

**Fix:** Either:
- (a) Move the default to `Directory.Build.props` so projects can override it, or
- (b) Add a condition: `Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''"` so it acts as a default only.

```xml
<!-- Option (a): Move to Directory.Build.props -->
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>

<!-- Option (b): Guarded default in .targets -->
<TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
```

### 3. `LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites instead of appending
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** all existing constants (including SDK defaults like `DEBUG` and `TRACE`) with only `ENABLE_LOGGING`. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:**
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

### 4. `LibA.csproj` — Unquoted condition value
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13

<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Fix:**

<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** In F#, file compilation order is significant — files can only reference types defined in files listed **above** them. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, meaning `Services.fs` cannot reference anything defined in `Domain.fs`. If `Services.fs` depends on domain types (the usual architecture), this will fail to compile.

**Fix:**

<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">

**Problem:** This is a legacy `packages.config`-style reference using a `HintPath` to a `packages/` folder. <PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">

<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>

<OutputPath>$(RepoRoot)artifacts\bin\LibA\</OutputPath>
```

## 🔴 Errors (Likely Broken or Causes Incorrect Behavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — TFM condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, line 10

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this solution), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK sets it from `<TargetFramework>` only after the project file's first `<PropertyGroup>` is processed. This condition will **never** be true, so documentation files are never generated despite the apparent intent.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, where `$(TargetFramework)` is populated:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Unconditional property overrides project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–10

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` is imported **after** the project file. Any unconditional property assignment here silently overwrites project-level values. LibB explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` but it is clobbered by this file.

**Fix:** Either:
- (a) Move the default to `Directory.Build.props` so projects can override it, or
- (b) Add a condition: `Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''"` so it acts as a default only.

```xml
<!-- Option (a): Move to Directory.Build.props -->
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>

<!-- Option (b): Guarded default in .targets -->
<TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
```

---

### 3. `LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites instead of appending
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** all existing constants (including SDK defaults like `DEBUG` and `TRACE`) with only `ENABLE_LOGGING`. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:**
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 4. `LibA.csproj` — Unquoted condition value
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The condition lacks quotes around both the property and value. If `Configuration` is empty, this evaluates as ` == Debug` which MSBuild may misparse or produce unexpected results.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

### 5. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — F# source file compilation order is wrong
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** In F#, file compilation order is significant — files can only reference types defined in files listed **above** them. `Services.fs` is listed before `Domain.fs`, meaning `Services.fs` cannot reference anything defined in `Domain.fs`. **Fix:**
```xml

<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```
